question: Your peace lily droops and yellows, though you water it every few days. What is killing it?
answer: Too much water. Roots need air as well as water; in soil that never drains they suffocate, rot and stop drinking. So an overwatered plant wilts exactly like a thirsty one, and the obvious cure, more water, finishes it. Water when the top few centimetres feel dry, in a pot with a hole.
move: A symptom can point two opposite ways; test before you give more.
ask: What am I giving more of because the problem looks like too little?

clues.text: Leaves hang limp, and the lower ones turn yellow, week after week.
No webs, no specks, nothing sticky under the leaves.
It sits near a bright window, and new leaves keep coming.
Push a finger into the pot: the soil is soggy two days after watering.
Tipped out, the roots are brown and mushy, and smell sour.

scene.why: A thirsty plant sits in dry soil. Wet soil under a wilting plant means the roots can't drink.

reference: https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/types/houseplants (Royal Horticultural Society, houseplant care: watering and root rot)
